doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Joining Dizzy Gillespie's quintet
summary: Moody joined the quintet in about 1956 after discussing with his wife, with Lalo Schifrin and later other pianists.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So you're living in -- back in New Jersey at this point?
Forest Hill [phonetic sp.], yes. So says, "Okay." So I joined Dizzy's quintet.

1950-something. 1956 or something. And Lalo Shiftman [phonetic sp.] was the piano player. Rudy Collins [phonetic sp.] the drummer, and Chris White [phonetic sp.] was [indiscernible]. Then Lalo left and -- and Dizzy asked -- and I said get Kenny [indiscernible], so Kenny [indiscernible] came with the group, you know. And then, when Kenny left, then Mike came with the group. Mike Longwell [phonetic sp.], you know. So.
